question: What simple test can prove two knots are different?
answer: The trefoil can be coloured with three colours so every crossing shows all-same or all-different strands, so it is tricolorable. Twists, pokes and slides never change this. A plain loop is one strand, so one colour only; no amount of moving turns the trefoil into a plain loop.
move: If one knot is tricolorable and another isn't, they're different knots.
